lesson.evidence: FFD, BFD, and complementary pairing all achieved optimal 8 bins. Random ordering produced 8-10 bins across 20 trials (avg 9.0). Items form perfect pairs (9+1, 8+2, 7+3, 6+4) filling capacity-10 exactly. Seed 0 random ordering created bin with weight 9, wasting capacity.
lesson.statement: When sixteen items form eight complementary pairs summing to bin capacity, weight-based ordering (FFD, BFD) achieves optimal packing; random ordering wastes capacity 19 of 20 trials.

summary: Compared FFD, BFD, complementary pairing, and 20 random orderings
All structured approaches achieved optimal 8 bins
Perfect complementary pairs fill capacity exactly
Final candidate verified: 8 bins, all items packed once, no overflow
